title: After a UNEP MARS alert, operators repair a failed ball valve that released 175 t of methane in one week at the Aerial oil and gas field, Alberta, a week after detection (April 2026)
summary: Trade press relaying UNEP's August 2026 snapshot: a 175 t/week methane plume at Alberta's Aerial field in April 2026 was traced to a failed ball valve on pigging equipment and repaired within a week.
account: The Chemical Engineer reported on 4 September 2026 that, in its monthly snapshot of the biggest satellite-detected methane plumes recorded in August, UNEP confirmed that operators had plugged a source at the Aerial oil and gas field in southeastern Alberta, Canada, which had released 175 t of methane (4,900 tCO2e) in a single week in April 2026. The cause was a failed ball valve connected to pigging equipment; operators completed the repair one week after the plume was first detected, following an alert issued under UNEP's Methane Alert and Response System (MARS). The article states that UNEP does not name suspected or known operators, and that since 2023 MARS has sent over 3,500 alerts but confirmed just 43 mitigation cases. UNEP's MARS page states that IMEO uses data from more than 30 satellite instruments coupled with scientific expertise and advanced AI models to notify governments and companies. The month-only date is recorded as the first of the month. The August 2026 UNEP snapshot itself was not fetched (the live snapshot link now serves the September 2026 update, which does not mention Canada), and unep.org press pages were unreachable for the earlier verifier, so the case rests on one trade-press report relaying UNEP.
purpose: Satellite-based detection and notification of large methane plumes so that operators mitigate them; this case was that purpose.
system: UNEP IMEO Methane Alert and Response System (MARS): satellite plume detection and analysis with AI models, notification and satellite confirmation
deployer: UNEP IMEO (notification); unnamed operators at the Aerial oil and gas field (repair)

taxonomy_note: Direct fit: a methane release stopped. ratings.reason: The operator found and fixed a failed valve releasing 175 t of methane a week within one week of detection; the operator is unnamed and no cost or further detail is reported.
A single confirmed case among about 43 since 2023 against more than 3,500 alerts; a one-week 4,900 tCO2e release stopped.

ai_role.statement: The report attributes the repair to a MARS alert and UNEP's confirmation; MARS detection and analysis are described as using satellites with advanced AI models only on UNEP's general page, so the AI contribution to this specific alert is not isolated. The event is documented by one news item relaying the system operator's snapshot, and the snapshot itself could not be fetched.
